articles.title: Beyond the paper: How AIResQ ClimSols is protecting urban India from flooding
articles.summary: Founded by Prof Udit Bhatia and Dr Divya Upadhyay, the venture combines physics-informed artificial intelligence with hydrological modelling to deliver hyperlocal, real-time flood intelligence, even where data is limited. articles.title: MP CM Mohan Yadav announces equal split of Rs 1 crore ex-gratia between kin

articles.title: Pakistan veterans Team withdraws from World Cup after PCB denies permission to Travel

articles.title: Russia’s S-500 Offer To India: Technology Transfer, Five S-400s And A Major Strategic
articles.summary: Russia may be offering India access to the S-500 Prometheus if New Delhi orders five additional S-400 systems. The reported package could include technology transfer, joint manufacturing and even re-export rights. The proposed S-400 order could be worth more than five billion dollars. India already has a 5. 4-billion-dollar agreement for five S-400 squadrons.

articles.title: Meghalaya to have highest number of football turfs in country: CM
articles.summary: Shillong, Oct 21: Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma on Wednesday said Meghalaya will become the state with the highest number of artificial football turf in India. Inaugurating the synthetic football turf at Mandalgitok Playground, Siju, the CM said the state is constructing 58 artificial turf grounds, one in each constituency, at over Rs 300 crore.
articles.title_hi: मेघालय में देश में सबसे अधिक फुटबॉल टर्फ होंगे: मुख्यमंत्री
articles.summary_hi: शिलांग, 21 अक्टूबर: मुख्यमंत्री कॉनराड के संगमा ने बुधवार को कहा कि मेघालय भारत में सबसे अधिक कृत्रिम फुटबॉल टर्फ वाला राज्य बन जाएगा। मंडलगिटोक खेल के मैदान, सिजू में सिंथेटिक फुटबॉल टर्फ का उद्घाटन करते हुए, सीएम ने कहा कि राज्य 300 करोड़ रुपये से अधिक की लागत से प्रत्येक निर्वाचन क्षेत्र में 58 कृत्रिम टर्फ मैदान का निर्माण कर रहा है।

articles.title: Great Indian Bustard chick killed by fox days after release in Rajasthan; rewilding
articles.summary: JAIPUR: A six-month-old male Great Indian Bustard (GIB) was killed by a fox just four days after being released into the wild at Desert National Park in Rajasthan’s Jaisalmer district on October 14. The bird was part of a government rewilding programme under which 11 captive-bred Great Indian Bustards were to be released into the wild.

articles.title: Jammu Kashmir Govt Assigns Additional Charge to Four District Information Officers
articles.summary: As per Government Order No. 53-JK (ID) of 2026, issued by the Information Department on October 21, Mukesh Kumar, Jr. JKAS, who is posted as DIO Reasi, will additionally oversee Doda district. articles.title: Indian Railways links Chhattisgarh’s Rowghat to national network for first time since
articles.summary: Indian Railways has connected Rowghat in Chhattisgarh to the national rail network for the first time since Independence. Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai flagged off two new passenger services Rowghat-Raipur and Raipur-Kurud as the Tadoki-Rowghat and Abhanpur-Kurud rail sections were inaugurated. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw also outlined plans to expand connectivity towards Rowghat, Jagdalpur and Visakhapatnam.

articles.title: Farmers Group Warns Modi Government Over Proposed United States Trade Deal
articles.summary: The All India Kisan Sabha warned the government of militant resistance on Wednesday if it proceeds with a proposed trade pact with the United States. The farmers organization claims the agreement threatens domestic agriculture, dairy producers, and rural sectors by exposing them to heavily subsidized foreign competition. The union urged officials to reject the deal.

articles.title: Communist Party of India Steps Up Campaign with Delhi Rally

The protest aims to mobilize workers, farmers, and students to demand policy changes addressing economic distress and defending constitutional rights across the country.

articles.title: Two new subterranean fish species discovered in Assam’s Goalpara
articles.summary: The newly identified species are Gitchak nakana, a tiny, transparent and blind loach, and Rakthamichthys anchi, a slender, eel-like fish belonging to the swamp eel family. According to Baruah, Gitchak nakana measures around two centimetres and appears reddish because its transparent body exposes its blood and internal organs. Rakthamichthys anchi, meanwhile, is adapted to life in underground groundwater environments.

articles.title: Ground below Uttarakhand quietly building energy for a mega earthquake: Study
articles.summary: The fault beneath the Uttarakhand Himalayas is strongly locked and accumulating tectonic strain, with the stored energy equivalent to that released by a magnitude 8. 1 earthquake approximately every 100 years, a new study has found. The research raises concerns about the long-term seismic potential of the central Himalayas, a region that scientists consider part of a major seismic gap.
